verdict_thresholds_M1.note: M0, M2 and M3 have no pass/fail gate.
verdict_thresholds_M1.basis: Spec section 4.5 verdict table: "at least 0.80 | close match"; "at least 0.50 and below 0.80 | partial match"; "below 0.50 | weak match". Text: "Verdict labels use M1 at `d_tol` = 10 m." Section 4.8: "verdict thresholds on M1: 0.80 and 0.50".

places.release: Mars 2020 Rover PLACES Bundle (PDS Geosciences Node), Release 16, posted 2026-08-11; sols 0 to 1897 in best_interp.csv (computed)

resampling.method: Both lines are built through cell centres (centre = outer corner + (index + 0.5) * pixel_size_m) and resampled at equal spacing along their length by linear interpolation in the local metre coordinates. The first and last vertex are kept at their exact positions; the last interval may be shorter than one pixel. Never interpolate in degrees. Method and spacing are written into report.json.

end_point_error_m.note: The report must state that end_point_error_m includes a cell-centre offset of up to about 0.71 pixel (0.71 m at 1.0 m per pixel): our route ends at cell centres, which can be up to half a pixel in each axis from the true point (sqrt(2)/2 pixel in the worst case).

results.caveat: Report every declared tolerance and metric, including bad results. No cherry-picking. The comparison is a sanity check, not ground truth; the rover traverse is not the optimal route for a person on foot.

limitations: the reference end point is on the bottom grid row, less than 1 m from the lower boundary, so the reference path leaves the grid there and does not stop naturally
